title: Publish: apply site migrations and set the site's database env on its Vercel project

notes: Decided 2026-10-20 after a live test on Otaku's Turso org (scratch DBs, deleted): a database token opens only its own database, and POST /databases/{db}/auth/rotate revokes only that database's tokens (another DB's token kept working). So: publish applies the version's db/migrations to the site DB (10m token), then sets SITE_DATABASE_URL, SITE_DATABASE_TOKEN (never-expiring, per-database) and a random per-site SITE_AUTH_SECRET as sensitive env on the site's Vercel project, once each. title: Site forms: add Turnstile (captcha) to the lead path
description: Lead forms today rely on a honeypot (fax), a 3 s minimum fill time and per-site/per-IP limits (packages/connect/src/site-leads.ts). Add Cloudflare Turnstile: the widget in components/lead-form.tsx (site key is public, can go in lib/locus.ts at publish), the token forwarded by the site's /api/lead route, and verified in submitSiteLead before the rate limits (secret key in Infisical, per deployment). Make it optional per site so sites without it keep working.
notes: Review of PR #63: Turnstile is the real fix for abuse of the per-site lead limits. The visitor IP (x-locus-visitor-ip) is caller-controlled, so spoofed IPs can spread past the per-IP limit and use up a site's allowance. Interim mitigation in site-leads.ts: junk (honeypot, too fast, invalid body) charges no limit; per-site is a 300/hour ceiling (logged when hit) plus a 20/minute burst guard. Verify the Turnstile token before any limit is charged.

description: A site published from staging bakes https://locus-git-staging-otaku-solutions.vercel.app/api/sites/<id>/leads, but staging is behind Vercel deployment protection: a POST there answers 401, so staging-published forms can't deliver leads and can't be tested end to end. The site's route can't send a bypass secret (no credential in site code). Options: exclude /api/sites/*/leads from protection if Vercel allows path exceptions, or test forms against production with a test sub-account.
close_reason: Not fixing: site forms were tested end to end on production (2026-10-20); site code can't carry a bypass secret, and staging stays behind Vercel protection.

title: Remove a deleted site's sandbox (RuntimeProvider destroy, also through the web app RPC)
description: deleteClientSite leaves the site's Vercel sandbox: it times out but its persistent filesystem stays on Otaku's team. Add destroy(key) to RuntimeProvider (Vercel, fake, remote RPC) and call it best-effort after the control delete.
close_reason: Deleting a site now deletes its Vercel sandbox and its own snapshots (RuntimeProvider.destroy, Vercel + fake). Site deletion runs in the web app, which has the Vercel provider directly, so no RPC op is needed.

title: Site sandbox credentials if the builder runs on the Coolify agent server (no Vercel OIDC there)
close_reason: Done by #68: the agent server on Coolify drives sandboxes through the web app's /api/internal/sandbox with a short agent-to-web token, so it needs no sandbox credential.

title: Site forms: only fill blanks on existing contacts
description: A lead form's contacts.upsert-contact matches an existing contact by email or phone and overwrites its name, phone and company with what the visitor typed (packages/connect/src/site-leads.ts sendToGhl; documented in the site-forms skill). Anyone who knows a customer's email can change those details. Change it so an existing contact only gets fields it has blank (e.g. look the contact up first, or upsert only email/phone and set the rest when empty), and put what the visitor typed in the note instead.
close_reason: Lead forms only fill an existing contact's blank fields; other typed details go in the note

title: Site forms: record each submission's outcome in the client's DB
description: submitSiteLead keeps no record: no table fits (control audit_log is for actors, and a lead must not live in the control DB; the tenant DB has no events table). Add a tenant table (site_lead_event: site_id, form, outcome accepted|dropped-honeypot|dropped-fast|rate-limited|ghl-error, ghl status, created_at; no visitor PII, no GHL ids since GHL is the system of record) via a tenant migration, write it with a per-request tenant token, and show counts on the Sites page so agencies can see forms working or failing.
close_reason: Delivered and failed leads are counted per site and day in the client DB (site_lead_day); spam isn't counted. The Sites page shows the last 30 days.

title: Site-builder tenant DB pool: retire idle connections, cap lease vs token life, keep original error if cleanup fails
close_reason: Pooled client DB connections close after 5 minutes unused; the 45 min pool lifetime vs 1 h token keeps 15 min for a late lease (documented). Close errors were already swallowed so they never replace a call's own error.

Guard buffers JSON bodies before Mastra's limit; host must cap size (documented) or add a cap in the guard. description: Threads are shared per client today (any member of the client can list, switch to and rename them); live sessions are per member. Decide whether threads should be private to the member who started them, and if so scope list/switch/rename by the thread's owner. From the PR #53 review.

title: Site forms: rotatable per-site form key instead of the public site id
description: Published sites post leads to /api/sites/<siteId>/leads. The site id is public and can't be revoked without changing the site. If a site's endpoint is ever abused, a per-site form key that can be rotated (and is re-baked into lib/locus.ts on publish) would let us cut it off. Split from locus-ptq.17.

title: Draft thread forgets its own steps after approval (wrong self-report)
description: Staging test 2026-10-25: after approval, the Conversations agent's summary said it drafted before reading the conversation. Evidence says it did read: the draft mentioned parking, which was only in an earlier message and never in the brief (ids only). The stored thread keeps only brief, an empty assistant message and the summary, so the run that resumes after the yes likely doesn't see its earlier read/propose steps. Check what the work-thread memory saves across an approval pause and make the resumed run see its tool calls (or stop it describing steps it can't see).
close_reason: Fixed: brief asks for the one-line summary before the send (own words survive the approval pause) and the not-kept note says later steps were taken with the result in view. Test in harness controller.test.ts.

title: After an approved send, the draft thread says the reply is still waiting for approval
description: Staging test 2026-10-26 (ABC Realty, live chat): the summary came first and the reply was approved and delivered, but the thread's final message said the reply 'won't go out until a person approves it'. The resumed run saw only GHL's answer to the send and took the call for the request to approve. Fix: perform_action results of changes that waited for a person carry an APPROVED note (kept in the stub), and the brief says a returned send has gone out.
close_reason: Fixed: approved perform_action results say they were approved and made; brief says a returned send was sent.

title: A write in the same model step as an untrusted read runs without approval
description: Found in review of #238: when the model calls query_data on untrusted content (form submissions, messages) and perform_action in the same step, requireApproval runs before the read taints the run, so the write goes through unasked. Pre-existing; check whether Mastra evaluates approvals per call before executing any, and gate writes in a step that also reads untrusted sources.

title: After an approved send, the draft thread takes back its own correct summary
description: Staging test 2026-10-26 04:09 UTC (ABC Realty, live chat, after #238): the reply was approved, sent and reported as sent, but the final message said the message text 'wasn't visible' and the summary was not taken from the conversation, and offered a correction. The read was real; on resume it is the NOT_KEPT stub. Fix: NOT_KEPT says a missing result is no sign of not having seen it, and the brief says after the send returns to say it was sent and not review what came before.
close_reason: Fixed: NOT_KEPT says absence is no sign of not having seen it; brief ends the run at the send.
